  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: center;"><b>Notes to Unaudited</b><b>&#160;</b><b>Condensed Consolidated Financial Statements</b></p>

  <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2025-07-01_2026-03-31" name="us-gaap:BusinessDescriptionAndBasisOfPresentationTextBlock" id="c3176949" escape="true">
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;"><b><em style="font: inherit;">1</em>)&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;Management Statement</b></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">As of <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026, </em>Standex International Corporation (&#8220;Standex&#8221; or the &#8220;Company&#8221;) is a diversified industrial manufacturer in&#160;<span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c144878143">four</span>&#160;broad business segments: Electronics, Aerospace &amp; Defense, Scientific, and Engraving &amp; Hydraulics&#160;with operations in the United States, Europe, Canada, Japan, Singapore, Mexico, Turkey,&#160;India, and China. The accompanying consolidated financial statements include the accounts of Standex International Corporation and its subsidiaries and are prepared in accordance with accounting principles generally accepted in the United States of America (&#8220;GAAP&#8221;). During the <em style="font: inherit;">third</em> quarter of fiscal <em style="font: inherit;">2026,</em> the Company sold its Federal Industries&#160;display merchandising business. This business was previously a part of the Specialty Solutions segment. Following this divestiture, the Company realigned its businesses and made organizational changes to better allocate&#160;resources to support changes to its business strategy. This resulted in&#160;combining&#160;Hydraulics business which was previously a part of the Specialty Solutions segment&#160;with the Engraving business to form the&#160;Engraving &amp; Hydraulics segment. Additionally, the&#160;Engineering Technologies segment was re-named as the Aerospace &amp; Defense segment to better reflect the markets served by this segment.&#160;Following these changes, the Company&#160;reviewed the quantitative and qualitative characteristics of its remaining businesses and determined that it&#160;has <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c144878146">four</span> reportable segments as noted in Note <em style="font: inherit;">16.</em> Accordingly, all periods presented have been revised to reflect the new reportable segments.&#160;The Other segment included in Note <em style="font: inherit;">16</em> includes the results of the Company's divested display merchandising business.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">All intercompany accounts and transactions have been eliminated in consolidation.&#160;Noncontrolling interests in subsidiaries related to Standex&#8217;s ownership interests of less than&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">100%</em>&#160;are reported as Noncontrolling interests in the consolidated balance sheets. The results of noncontrolling ownership interests held by Standex are reported as Net income attributable to redeemable noncontrolling interests in the consolidated statements of operations.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">The Company considers events or transactions that occur after the balance sheet date, but before the financial statements are issued to provide additional evidence relative to certain estimates or to identify matters that require additional disclosure. The Company&#160;evaluated subsequent events through the date and time the consolidated financial statements were issued.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">In the opinion of management, the accompanying unaudited condensed consolidated financial statements contain all adjustments necessary to present fairly the results of operations for the <em style="font: inherit;">three</em> and <em style="font: inherit;">nine</em> months ended <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026 </em>and <em style="font: inherit;">2025</em>, the cash flows for the <em style="font: inherit;">nine</em>&#160;months ended <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026 </em>and <em style="font: inherit;">2025</em>, and the financial position of Standex&#160;at <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026</em>. The interim results are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> necessarily indicative of results for a full year. The accompanying&#160;unaudited condensed consolidated financial statements have been prepared pursuant to the rules and regulations of the Securities and Exchange Commission. Certain information and note disclosures normally included in annual financial statements prepared in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles have been condensed or omitted pursuant to those rules and regulations, although the Company believes that the disclosures made are adequate to make the information <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> misleading. The unaudited condensed consolidated financial statements and notes do <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> contain information which would substantially duplicate the disclosures contained in the audited annual consolidated financial statements and notes for the year ended <em style="font: inherit;"> June 30, 2025</em>. The condensed consolidated balance sheet at <em style="font: inherit;"> June 30, 2025</em>&#160;presented herein was derived from audited financial statements, but does <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> include all disclosures required by accounting principles generally accepted in the United States of America. The financial statements contained herein should be read in conjunction with the Annual Report on Form <em style="font: inherit;">10</em>-K and in particular, the audited consolidated financial statements for the year ended <em style="font: inherit;"> June 30, 2025</em>.&#160;Unless otherwise noted, references to years are to the Company&#8217;s fiscal years.&#160;Currently the&#160;fiscal year end is <em style="font: inherit;"> June 30.&#160;</em>For further clarity, the Company's&#160;fiscal year <em style="font: inherit;">2026</em>&#160;includes the <em style="font: inherit;">twelve</em>-month period from <em style="font: inherit;"> July 1, 2025&#160;</em>to <em style="font: inherit;"> June 30, 2026.</em></p>

   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">The preparation of consolidated financial statements in conformity with GAAP requires the use of estimates, judgments and assumptions that affect the reported amounts of assets, liabilities, revenues and expenses, and related disclosure of contingent assets and liabilities at the date of the financial statements and for the period then ended. Estimates are based on historical experience, actuarial estimates, current conditions and various other assumptions that are believed to be reasonable under the circumstances. These estimates form the basis for making judgments about the carrying values of assets and liabilities when they are&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">not</em>&#160;readily apparent from other sources. These estimates assist in the identification and assessment of the accounting treatment necessary with respect to commitments and contingencies. Changes in underlying assumptions or conditions could cause estimates to differ which would impact the financial statements. The estimates and assumptions used in the preparation of the consolidated financial statements have considered the implications on the Company of ongoing global events and related economic impacts. As a result, there is heightened volatility and uncertainty around tariff actions, supply chain performance, labor availability, and customer demand. However, the magnitude of such impact on the Company&#8217;s business and its duration is uncertain. The Company is <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> aware of any specific event or circumstance that would require an update to its estimates or adjustments to the carrying value of its assets and liabilities as of&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026</em> and the issuance date of this quarterly report&#160;on Form <em style="font: inherit;">10</em>-Q.</p>

   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><span style="text-decoration: underline; ">Recently Issued Accounting Pronouncements</span></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">From time to time, new accounting pronouncements are issued by the FASB or other standard setting bodies that the Company&#160;adopts as of the specified effective date.&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">The Organization for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) and the <em style="font: inherit;">G20</em> Inclusive Framework on Base Erosion and Profit Shifting (the "Inclusive Framework") have put forth Pillar Two proposals that ensure a minimal level of taxation. Several countries in which the Company operates, including several European Union member states, have adopted domestic legislation to implement the Inclusive Framework's global corporate minimum tax rate of <em style="font: inherit;">fifteen</em> percent. This legislation became effective for the Company beginning in the fiscal year <em style="font: inherit;">2025.</em>&#160;In <em style="font: inherit;"> January 2026, </em>the OECD issued additional guidance on the Pillar Two system of global minimum tax rules. Based on the Company's analysis of Pillar Two provisions, these tax law changes are&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">not</em> expected to have a material impact on the Company's financial statements for the fiscal year <em style="font: inherit;">2026.</em></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <div style="font-size: 10pt; text-indent: 0pt; text-align: justify;">
     In
    <em style="font: inherit;"> July 2025, </em>the U.S. government enacted The One Big Beautiful Bill Act of
    <em style="font: inherit;">2025</em> which includes, among other provisions, changes to the U.S. corporate income tax system including the allowance of immediate expensing of qualifying research and development expenses and permanent extensions of certain provisions within the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act. Certain provisions were effective for Standex beginning
    <em style="font: inherit;"> June 1, 2025. </em>Based on the Company's current analysis of the provisions, the Company does
    <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> expect these tax law changes to have a material impact on the Company's financial statements.&#160;The Company will continue to evaluate the&#160;impact of these provisions throughout the remainder of the year.

    <em style="font: inherit;">2023</em>-
    <em style="font: inherit;">09,</em> Income Taxes (Topic
    <em style="font: inherit;">740</em>) - Improvements to Income Tax Disclosures. This ASU was issued to enhance the transparency and decision usefulness of income tax disclosures by requiring public business entities on an annual basis to disclose specific categories in the rate reconciliation, additional information for reconciling items that meet a quantitative threshold, and certain information about income taxes paid. This ASU is effective for fiscal years beginning after
    <em style="font: inherit;"> December 15, 2024. </em>The amendments in this ASU are required to be applied on a prospective basis and retrospective adoption is permitted. The Company is&#160;currently evaluating the impact that the adoption of ASU
    <em style="font: inherit;">2023</em>-
    <em style="font: inherit;">09</em> will have&#160;on its&#160;consolidated financial statements and disclosures.

    <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">In&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> November 2024,&#160;</em>the FASB issued ASU&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2024</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">03,</em>&#160;Income Statement - Reporting Comprehensive Income (Topic&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">220</em>): Expense Disaggregation Disclosures. This ASU also requires, in the notes to the financial statements, disclosure of specified information about certain costs and expenses which includes purchases of inventory, employee compensation, depreciation, and intangible asset amortization included in each relevant expense caption. ASU&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2025</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">01</em>&#160;is effective for fiscal years beginning after&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> December 15, 2026,&#160;</em>and interim periods within annual reporting periods beginning after&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> December 15, 2027,&#160;</em>on a retrospective or prospective basis, with early adoption permitted. This ASU will be effective for the Company&#8217;s Form&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">10</em>-K for fiscal&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2028</em>&#160;and Form&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">10</em>-Q filed thereafter. This ASU&#160;introduces <em style="font: inherit;">five</em> targeted improvements to better align hedge accounting with entities&#8217; risk management activities.&#160;This ASU is effective for fiscal years&#160;beginning after <em style="font: inherit;"> December 15, 2026, </em>and interim periods within those annual reporting periods, with early adoption permitted. The amendments in this ASU are required to be applied on a prospective basis for all hedging relationships. The Company&#160;is currently evaluating the impact this ASU&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> may&#160;</em>have on its&#160;financial statement disclosures.</p>

    <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt;">In <em style="font: inherit;"> September 2025, </em>the FASB issued ASU&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2025</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">06,</em>&#160;Intangibles&#8212;Goodwill and Other&#8212;Internal-Use Software (Subtopic <em style="font: inherit;">350</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">40</em>): Targeted Improvements to the Accounting for Internal-Use Software&#160;related to accounting for internal-use software costs. The amendments in this update improve the operability of the guidance by removing all references to software development project stages so that the guidance is neutral to different software development methods. This update is effective for annual periods beginning after <em style="font: inherit;"> December 15, 2027, </em>including interim periods within those fiscal years, though early adoption is permitted. The Company is currently in the process of evaluating the effects of this pronouncement on its&#160;consolidated financial statements.</p>

The guidance in ASU <em style="font: inherit;">2025</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">11</em> amends ASC Topic <em style="font: inherit;">270,</em> Interim Reporting, to provide clarity on the current interim reporting requirements and to require&#160;entities to disclose events since the end of the last annual reporting period that have a material impact on the entity through the addition of the disclosure principle. Upon adoption, ASU <em style="font: inherit;">2025</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">11</em> <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>be applied prospectively or retrospectively.    <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><span style="text-decoration: underline; "><b>Amran/Narayan Group</b></span></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">On&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> October 28, 2024 (</em>&#8220;Closing Date&#8221;), the Company acquired, in separate transactions,&#160;<ix:nonFraction id="c144878237" contextRef="i_2024-10-28_BusinessAcquisitionAxis-AmranInstrumentTransformersMember" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:BusinessAcquisitionPercentageOfVotingInterestsAcquired" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="0">100</ix:nonFraction>% of the outstanding membership interest in Amran LLC (&#8220;Amran&#8221;), a privately-held company based in Houston, Texas, pursuant to a Securities Purchase Agreement (the &#8220;Amran Purchase Agreement&#8221;) and through its wholly owned subsidiary, Mold-Tech Singapore PTE LTD (&#8220;Mold-Tech Singapore&#8221;),&#160;<ix:nonFraction id="c144878238" contextRef="i_2024-10-28_BusinessAcquisitionAxis-NarayanPowertechPvtLtdMember" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:BusinessAcquisitionPercentageOfVotingInterestsAcquired" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="3">90.1</ix:nonFraction>% of the capital stock of Narayan Powertech Private Limited (&#8220;Narayan&#8221;), a privately-held India-based company, pursuant to a Securities Purchase Agreement (the &#8220;Narayan Purchase Agreement&#8221;) (collectively the &#8220;Amran/Narayan Group&#8221;). With manufacturing locations in the United States and India, Amran/Narayan Group is a leading manufacturer of low voltage and medium voltage instrument transformers. Its custom product portfolio is specifically designed and developed in partnership with OEMs for their specific equipment related to electrical grid applications. This acquisition continues the Company's&#160;portfolio strategy of focusing its&#160;higher-margin business segments in faster-growing markets. Amran/Narayan Group results are reported within the Company's Electronics segment.</p>
   <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">Total consideration for Amran aggregated to $<ix:nonFraction id="c144878239" contextRef="d_2024-10-28_2024-10-28_BusinessAcquisitionAxis-AmranInstrumentTransformersMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:BusinessCombinationConsiderationTransferred1" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">179.7</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million, consisting of $<ix:nonFraction id="c144878240" contextRef="d_2024-10-28_2024-10-28_BusinessAcquisitionAxis-AmranInstrumentTransformersMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:PaymentsToAcquireBusinessesGross" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">153.7</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million in cash consideration and&#160;<ix:nonFraction id="c144878241" contextRef="d_2024-10-28_2024-10-28_BusinessAcquisitionAxis-AmranInstrumentTransformersMember_EquityInterestIssuedOrIssuableByTypeAxis-CommonStockMember" unitRef="Share" name="us-gaap:BusinessAcquisitionEquityInterestsIssuedOrIssuableNumberOfSharesIssued" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">152,299</ix:nonFraction>&#160;shares of Standex common stock, issued out of the Company's treasury shares, with a fair value of $<ix:nonFraction id="c144878242" contextRef="d_2024-10-28_2024-10-28_BusinessAcquisitionAxis-AmranInstrumentTransformersMember_EquityInterestIssuedOrIssuableByTypeAxis-TreasuryStockCommonMember" unitRef="Share" name="us-gaap:BusinessAcquisitionEquityInterestsIssuedOrIssuableNumberOfSharesIssued" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">26.0</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million. The fair value of Standex common stock issued as part of the consideration for Amran was determined on the basis of the closing market price of the Company's common shares on the Closing Date. The total consideration for the&#160;<ix:nonFraction id="c144878243" contextRef="i_2024-10-28_BusinessAcquisitionAxis-NarayanPowertechPvtLtdMember" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:BusinessAcquisitionPercentageOfVotingInterestsAcquired" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="3">90.1</ix:nonFraction>% interest in Narayan consisted of a cash payment of $<ix:nonFraction id="c144878244" contextRef="d_2024-10-28_2024-10-28_BusinessAcquisitionAxis-NarayanPowertechPvtLtdMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:PaymentsToAcquireBusinessesGross" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">261.9</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million.&#160;The Company entered into a Shareholder Agreement&#160;that provides the Company with the right to purchase, and the noncontrolling interest holders with the right to sell, their remaining noncontrolling interest at a contractually defined redemption value. As the redemptions are contingently redeemable at the option of the noncontrolling interest shareholders, the Company classifies the redeemable noncontrolling interest in the mezzanine equity section on the consolidated balance sheets, which is presented above the equity section and below liabilities. The repurchase price of the redeemable noncontrolling interests is the greater of the share price paid for similar shares as part of the Narayan Acquisition or&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">12</em>&#160;times&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">twelve</em>&#160;months' trailing EBITDA.&#160;The redeemable noncontrolling interest represents the minority shareholder's&#160;interest.&#160;More specifically, the Shareholders&#8217; Agreement provides the noncontrolling interest holders with the right&#160;(but&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">not</em>&#160;an obligation) to transfer up to their remaining interest in Narayan for a period of&#160;<span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c144878249">three</span>&#160;years ("Put Option Period") to Mold-Tech Singapore. Subsequent to the expiration of the Put Option Period, Mold-Tech Singapore will have the right (but&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">not</em>&#160;an obligation) to acquire the remaining interest in Narayan for an additional&#160;<span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c144878251">three</span>-year consecutive period.</p>

Goodwill of $<ix:nonFraction id="c144878259" contextRef="i_2024-10-28_BusinessAcquisitionAxis-NarayanPowertechPvtLtdMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:Goodwill" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">298.4</ix:nonFraction>&#160;was recognized. Goodwill related to the Amran (U.S.) acquisition is deductible for U.S. income tax purposes; the goodwill&#160;related to the Narayan (India) acquisition is <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> deductible. The accounting for business combinations requires estimates and judgments regarding expectations for future cash flows of the acquired business, and the allocations of those cash flows to identifiable tangible and intangible assets, in determining the assets acquired and liabilities assumed. The fair values assigned to tangible and intangible assets acquired and liabilities assumed are based on management's best estimates and assumptions, as well as other information compiled by management, including valuations that utilize customary valuation procedures and techniques. On the date of acquisition, the fair value of the noncontrolling interest in Narayan was determined based on the consideration expected to be transferred by the Company for its controlling ownership interest based on the Standex share price at the Closing Date.</p>

   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">With respect to each of the McStarlite and Amran/Narayan Group acquisitions, the estimated fair values of the indefinite lived tradenames were determined based on an income approach using the relief from royalty method, which assumes that, in lieu of ownership, a&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">third</em>&#160;party would be willing to pay a royalty in order to exploit the related benefits of the tradenames assets. The cash flow projections the Company uses to estimate the fair value of the tradenames intangible assets involve&#160;several assumptions, including projected revenue growth, an estimated royalty rate, after-tax royalty savings expected from ownership of the tradenames, and a discount rate used to derive the estimated fair value of the tradenames.&#160; The estimated fair value of the customer relationships intangible assets were determined based on the income approach using the multi-period excess earnings method, which measures the economic benefit indirectly by calculating the income attributable to an asset after appropriate returns are paid to complementary assets used in conjunction with the subject asset to produce the earnings associated with the subject asset, commonly referred to as contributory asset charges.&#160; The fair value determination of the customer relationships intangible asset required the Company&#160;to make significant estimates and assumptions related to future cash flows and the selection of an appropriate discount rate to apply to future cash flows.</p>

   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><i>Deal&#160;Related Costs</i></p>

   <p style="margin: 0pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; text-align: justify;">Deal&#160;related costs include costs related to acquired businesses and other pending acquisitions. These costs consist of (i) deferred compensation arrangements and (ii) deal&#160;related professional service fees and expenses, including financial advisory, legal, accounting, and other outside services incurred in connection with integration and acquisition activities, and regulatory matters related to acquired entities. These costs do <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> include purchase accounting expenses, which the Company&#160;defines as acquired backlog and the step-up of inventory to fair value, or the amortization of the acquired intangible assets.</p>

  <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2025-07-01_2026-03-31" name="us-gaap:RevenueFromContractWithCustomerTextBlock" id="c3176954" escape="true">
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;"><b><em style="font: inherit;">3</em>)&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;Revenue From Contracts With Customers </b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">Most of the Company&#8217;s contracts have a single performance obligation which represents the product or service being sold to the customer. Some contracts include multiple performance obligations such as a product and the related installation and/or extended warranty. Additionally, most of the Company&#8217;s contracts offer assurance type warranties in connection with the sale of a product to customers. Assurance type warranties provide a customer with assurance that the product complies with agreed-upon specifications. Assurance type warranties do <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> represent a separate performance obligation.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">In general, the Company recognizes revenue at the point in time control transfers to its customer based on predetermined shipping terms. Revenue is recognized over time under certain long-term contracts within the Aerospace &amp; Defense and Engraving &amp; Hydraulics segments for highly customized customer products that have <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> alternative use and in which the contract specifies the Company has a right to payment for its costs, plus a reasonable margin. For these products,&#160;the transfer of control is measured pro rata, based upon current estimates of costs to complete such contracts. Losses on contracts are fully recognized in the period in which the losses become determinable. Revisions in profit estimates are reflected on a cumulative basis in the period in which the basis for such revision becomes known.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">&#160;</p>

   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;"><i>Contract Balances</i></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">Contract assets represent&#160;revenue recognized related to work completed but <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> yet billed as of the reporting date. Contract liabilities are customer deposits for which revenue has <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> been recognized. Current contract liabilities are recorded as accrued liabilities.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">The timing of revenue recognition, invoicing and cash collections results in billed receivables, contract assets and contract liabilities on the consolidated balance sheets. When consideration is received from a customer prior to transferring goods or services to the customer under the terms of a contract, a contract liability is recorded. Contract liabilities are recognized as revenue after control of the goods and services are transferred to the customer and all revenue recognition criteria have been met.&#160;Contract liabilities as of&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026</em> and&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> June 30, 2025</em> were $<ix:nonFraction id="c144878357" contextRef="i_2026-03-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:ContractWithCustomerLiability" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">0.4</ix:nonFraction> million&#160;and $<ix:nonFraction id="c144878358" contextRef="i_2025-06-30" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:ContractWithCustomerLiability" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">5.2</ix:nonFraction> million, respectively.</p>

   <p style="font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; font-family: Times New Roman;"><b><em style="font: inherit;">4</em>) &#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;Fair Value Measurements</b></p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;"><b>&#160;</b></p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">The financial instruments shown below are presented at fair value. Fair value is defined as the price that would be received to sell an asset or paid to transfer a liability in an orderly transaction between market participants at the measurement date. Where available, fair value is based on observable market prices or parameters or derived from such prices or parameters. Where observable prices or inputs are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> available, valuation models <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>be applied.</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <ix:exclude>
    <div class="PGFTR" style="text-align: center; width: 100%">
     <div class="hf-row">
      <div class="hf-cell PGNUM" style="text-align: center; font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times New Roman;">
       <em style="font: inherit;">18</em>
      </div>
     </div>
    </div>
    <hr style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: always; border: none; width: 100%; height: 2px; color: #000000; background-color: #000000"/>
    <div class="PGHDR" style="text-align: left; width: 100%">
     <div class="hf-row">
      <div class="hf-cell TOCLink">
        &#160;
      </div>
     </div>
    </div>
   </ix:exclude>
   <ix:exclude>&#160;</ix:exclude>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">Assets and liabilities recorded at fair value in the consolidated balance sheet are categorized based upon the level of judgment associated with the inputs used to measure their fair values. Hierarchical levels directly related to the amount of subjectivity associated with the inputs to fair valuation of these assets and liabilities and the methodologies used in valuation are as follows:</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 36pt; text-align: justify;">Level <em style="font: inherit;">1</em> &#8211; Quoted prices (unadjusted) in active markets for identical assets and liabilities. The Company&#8217;s deferred compensation plan assets consist of shares in various mutual funds (investments are participant-directed) which invest in a broad portfolio of debt and equity securities. These assets are valued based on publicly quoted market prices for the funds&#8217; shares as of the balance sheet dates.</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 36pt; text-align: justify;">Level <em style="font: inherit;">2</em> &#8211; Inputs, other than quoted prices in an active market, that are observable either directly or indirectly through correlation with market data. For foreign exchange forward contracts and interest rate swaps, the Company values the instruments based on the market price of instruments with similar terms, which are based on spot and forward rates as of the balance sheet dates. The Company has considered the creditworthiness of counterparties in valuing all assets and liabilities.</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 36pt; text-align: justify;">Level <em style="font: inherit;">3</em> &#8211; Unobservable inputs based upon the Company&#8217;s best estimate of what market participants would use in pricing the asset or liability.&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">There were <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> transfers of assets or liabilities between any levels of the fair value measurement hierarchy at <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026</em>&#160;or&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> June 30, 2025</em>.&#160;The Company&#8217;s policy is to recognize transfers between levels as of the date they occur.</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">Cash and cash equivalents, accounts receivable,&#160;accounts payable, and debt are carried at cost, which approximates fair value.</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">&#160;</p>

   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 8pt; text-align: justify;"><sup style="vertical-align:top;line-height:120%;">(a)</sup>&#160;The Company&#8217;s financial liabilities based upon Level&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">3</em>&#160;inputs comprise of contingent consideration arrangement relating to its acquisition of&#160;SEPL in the event that certain financial targets are achieved during the&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">two</em>&#160;years following its acquisition&#160;in the&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">fourth</em>&#160;quarter of fiscal year&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2024.</em>&#160;The Company has determined the fair value of the liabilities for the contingent consideration based on an evaluation of&#160;the probability and amount of any deferred compensation that has been earned to date. This fair value measurement is based on significant inputs&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">not</em>&#160;observable in the market and thus represents a Level&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">3</em>&#160;measurement within the fair value hierarchy. The fair value of the contingent consideration liability associated with future payments was based on several factors, the most significant of which are typically the financial performance of the acquired business and the risk-adjusted discount rate for the fair value measurement.&#160;During the&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">nine</em> months ended <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026</em>, the reduction in the fair value of the contingent consideration liability was a result of the Company&#8217;s payment of $<ix:nonFraction id="c144878477" contextRef="d_2025-07-01_2026-03-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:PaymentForContingentConsiderationLiabilityFinancingActivities" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">0.3</ix:nonFraction> million pursuant to the SEPL agreement.&#160;</p>

This was recorded as investments within other non-current assets in the consolidated balance sheets to reflect the initial fair value of the stock acquired. These investments are recorded using either the equity method of accounting or the cost minus impairment adjusted for observable price changes, depending on ownership percentage and other factors that suggest significant influence. The Company concluded it does&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">not</em>&#160;have a significant ownership percentage or influence. The Company monitors these&#160;investments to evaluate whether any increase or decline in the value has occurred, based on the implied value of recent company financings, public market prices of comparable companies and general market conditions.&#160;</p>

    <div style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt;">
     <span style="background-color:null">The expected cost associated with warranty obligations on our products is recorded as a component of cost of sales when the revenue is recognized. The Company&#8217;s estimate of warranty cost is based on contract terms and historical warranty loss experience that is periodically adjusted for recent actual experience. Since warranty estimates are forecasts based on the best available information, claims costs <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>differ from amounts provided. Adjustments to initial obligations for warranties are made as changes in the obligations become reasonable to&#160;estimate.</span>

   <p style="margin: 0pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><b style="font-size: 10pt; text-align: justify;"><em style="font: inherit;">10</em>) </b><b style="font-size: 10pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;</b><b style="font-size: 10pt; text-align: justify;">Derivative Financial Instruments</b></p>
   <p style="margin: 0pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 9pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="margin: 0pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">Information about the Company&#8217;s derivative financial instruments is as follows:</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><i>Interest Rate Swaps</i></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 9pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">From time to time as dictated by market opportunities, the Company enters into interest rate swap agreements designed to manage exposure to interest rates on the Company&#8217;s variable rate indebtedness. The Company recognizes all derivatives on its consolidated balance sheets at fair value. The Company&#160;designates&#160;its interest rate swap agreements, including those that <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>be forward-dated, as cash flow hedges, and changes in the fair value of the swaps are recognized in accumulated other comprehensive income until the hedged items are recognized in earnings. Hedge ineffectiveness, if any, associated with the swaps is reported in earnings within interest expense.</p>
   <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&#160;</p>

   <p style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; margin: 0pt;"><b style="font-size: 10pt;"><em style="font: inherit;">12</em></b><b style="font-size: 10pt;">)&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;Income Taxes</b></p>
   <div style="font-size:10pt">
    <div style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; margin: 0pt;">
      &#160;
    </div>
   </div>
   <div style="font-size:10pt">
    <div style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; text-align: justify;">
     <p style="margin: 0pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">The Company's effective tax rate from continuing operations for the&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">three</em> and <em style="font: inherit;">nine</em> months ended&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026</em>&#160;was&#160;<ix:nonFraction id="c144878829" contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:EffectiveIncomeTaxRateContinuingOperations" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="2">17.0</ix:nonFraction>%&#160;and&#160;<ix:nonFraction id="c144878830" contextRef="d_2025-07-01_2026-03-31" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:EffectiveIncomeTaxRateContinuingOperations" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="3">19.7</ix:nonFraction>%,&#160;respectively, compared with&#160;-<ix:nonFraction id="c144878831" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-03-31" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:EffectiveIncomeTaxRateContinuingOperations" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="3" sign="-">29.6</ix:nonFraction>% and&#160;<ix:nonFraction id="c144878832" contextRef="d_2024-07-01_2025-03-31" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:EffectiveIncomeTaxRateContinuingOperations" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="3">1.1</ix:nonFraction>%&#160;for the equivalent prior year periods, respectively.&#160;</p>
     <p style="margin: 0pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&#160;</p>
     <p style="margin: 0pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">The tax rate was impacted in the <em style="font: inherit;">three</em> and <em style="font: inherit;">nine</em> months ended&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026</em> by the following items:&#160;(i) the recognition of a discrete tax benefit of approximately $<ix:nonFraction id="c144878835" contextRef="d_2025-07-01_2026-03-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:IncomeTaxReconciliationChangeInDeferredTaxAssetsValuationAllowance" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-6">6</ix:nonFraction> million related to the release of a valuation allowance previously recorded against the capital loss carryforward deferred tax asset, due to the utilization of such carryforward in connection with the divestiture of Federal Industries; (ii) changes in the geographic mix of earnings; (iii) foreign withholding taxes; and (iv) federal tax credits related to research and development activities.</p>
     <p style="margin: 0pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&#160;</p>
     <p style="margin: 0pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">The tax rate was impacted in the <em style="font: inherit;">three</em> and <em style="font: inherit;">nine</em> months ended&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2025</em> by the following items:&#160;(i) a discrete tax benefit related to the release of a previously recorded tax reserve for a <em style="font: inherit;">one</em>-time tax charge on historical foreign earnings, as the relevant statute of limitations expired during the quarter; (ii) the jurisdictional mix of earnings; (iii) foreign withholding taxes; and (iv) federal research and development tax credits.</p>

   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;"><b><em style="font: inherit;">15</em></b><b>)&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;Contingencies</b></p>

   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">From time to time, the Company is subject to various claims and legal proceedings, including claims related to environmental remediation, either asserted or unasserted, that arise in the ordinary course of business. While the outcome of these proceedings and claims cannot be predicted with certainty, the Company&#8217;s management does&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">not</em>&#160;believe that the outcome of any of the currently existing legal matters will have a material impact on the Company&#8217;s consolidated financial position, results of operations or cash flow. The Company accrues for losses related to a claim or litigation when the Company&#8217;s management considers a potential loss probable and can reasonably estimate such potential loss.</p>

materially adverse or unanticipated legal judgments, fines, penalties or settlements; conditions in the financial and banking markets, including fluctuations in exchange rates and the inability to repatriate foreign cash; domestic and international economic conditions, including the impact, length and degree of economic downturns on the customers and markets we serve and more specifically conditions in the automotive, construction, aerospace, defense, transportation, food service equipment, consumer appliance, energy, oil and gas and general industrial markets; lower-cost competition; the relative mix of products which impact margins and operating efficiencies in certain of our businesses; the impact of higher raw material and component costs, particularly steel, certain materials used in electronics parts, petroleum based products, and refrigeration components;   <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;"><b>Overview</b></p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;"><b>&#160;</b></p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">We are a diversified industrial manufacturer with leading positions in a variety of products and services that are used in diverse commercial and industrial markets. We are&#160;headquartered in Salem, New Hampshire.&#160;Our businesses work in close partnership with our customers to deliver custom solutions or engineered components that solve their unique and specific needs, an approach we call "Customer Intimacy".&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">On March 9, 2026, we completed the divestiture of Federal Industries to a third party for cash proceeds of&#160;$68.3 million. The divestiture supports continued portfolio simplification and enables us to focus on larger businesses and fast growth end market opportunities. Post the divestiture, the&#160;Hydraulics business was combined with the Engraving business under the Engraving &amp; Hydraulics segment and the Engineering Technologies segment has been re-named as the Aerospace &amp; Defense segment. We believe that this name change will improve understanding of the business and its end markets. As a result, the Company will now report under the four operating segments of Electronics, Aerospace &amp; Defense, Scientific, and Engraving &amp; Hydraulics.&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">Our long-term business strategy&#160;is to create, improve, and enhance shareholder value by building more profitable, focused industrial platforms through our Standex Value Creation System.&#160;This methodology&#160;employs four components: Balanced Performance Plan, Growth Disciplines, Operational Excellence, and Talent Management and provides both&#160;a company-wide framework and tools used to achieve our goals.&#160;We intend to continue investing organically and inorganically in high margin and growth businesses using this balanced and proven approach.&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">It is our objective to grow larger and more profitable business units through a commitment to both organic and inorganic initiatives. We have a particular focus on identifying and investing in businesses, new products and new applications that complement our existing&#160;products and will increase our overall scale, global presence and capabilities.&#160;We continue to pursue&#160;acquisitions that are&#160;strategically aligned with our businesses and where the opportunity meets our investment metrics. We&#160;have divested, and likely will continue to divest, businesses that are not strategic or do not meet our growth and return expectations.</p>
  <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">As&#160;a result of our&#160;portfolio moves over the past several years, we have transformed Standex to a company with a more focused group of businesses selling customized solutions to high value end markets via a compelling customer value proposition.&#160; The narrowing of the portfolio allows for greater management focus on driving operational disciplines and positions us well to use our cash flow from operations to invest selectively in our ongoing pipeline of organic and inorganic opportunities.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">The Company&#8217;s strong historical cash flow has been a cornerstone for funding our capital allocation strategy.&#160;We use cash flow generated from operations to fund investments in capital assets to upgrade our facilities, improve productivity and lower costs, invest in the strategic growth programs described above, including organic growth, and to return cash to our shareholders through payment of dividends and stock buybacks.&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">Restructuring expenses reflect costs associated with our&#160;efforts of continuously improving operational efficiency and expanding globally in order to remain competitive in our end user markets.&#160;We incur costs for actions to size our businesses to a level appropriate for current economic conditions, improve our cost structure, enhance our competitive position and increase operating margins.&#160;Such expenses include costs for moving facilities to locations that allow for lower fixed and variable costs, external consultants who provide additional expertise starting up plants after relocation, downsizing operations because of changing economic conditions, and other costs resulting from asset redeployment decisions.&#160;Shutdown costs include severance, benefits, stay bonuses, lease and contract terminations, asset write-downs, costs of moving fixed assets, and moving and relocation costs. Vacant facility costs include maintenance, utilities, property taxes and other costs.</p>
  <p style="text-align: justify; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="text-align: justify; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt;">Because of the diversity of the Company&#8217;s businesses, end user markets and geographic locations, management does not use specific external indices to predict the future performance of the Company, other than general information about broad macroeconomic trends.&#160; Each of our individual business units serves niche markets and attempts to identify trends other than general business and economic conditions which are specific to its business and which could impact its performance.&#160;Those units report pertinent information to senior management, which uses it to the extent relevant to assess the future performance of the Company.&#160;A description of any such material trends is described below in the applicable segment analysis.</p>
  <p style="text-align: justify; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt;">&#160;</p>

  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">We monitor a number of key performance indicators (&#8220;KPIs&#8221;) including net sales, income from operations, backlog, effective income tax rate, gross profit margin, and operating cash flow. A discussion of these KPIs is included below.&#160;We may also supplement the discussion of these KPIs by identifying the impact of foreign exchange rates, acquisitions, and other significant items when they have a material impact on a specific KPI.&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">We believe the discussion of these items provides enhanced information to investors by disclosing their impact on the overall trend which provides a clearer comparative view of the KPI, as applicable.&#160; For discussion of the impact of foreign exchange rates on KPIs, we&#160;calculate&#160;the impact as the difference between the current period KPI calculated at the current period exchange rate as compared to the KPI calculated at the historical exchange rate for the prior period.&#160; For discussion of the impact of acquisitions or divestitures, we isolate the effect on the KPI amount that would have existed regardless of such acquisition or divestiture.&#160; Sales resulting from synergies between the acquisition and existing operations of the Company are considered organic growth for the purposes of our discussion.</p>

  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><b>Net Sales</b></p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">Net sales&#160;increased in the third quarter of fiscal year 2026&#160;by $16.8&#160;million or 8.1%, when compared to the prior year quarter.&#160;Acquisitions accounted for increased sales of&#160;$3.3 million&#160;or 1.6%. Divestitures reduced sales by&#160;$2.9 million, or 1.4%.&#160;Foreign currency positively impacted sales by&#160;$2.9&#160;million, or&#160;1.4%.&#160;Organic sales increased $13.5&#160;million, or 6.5%, primarily due to&#160;increased sales into fast growth markets and contributions from new products.</p>
  <div style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; text-align: justify;">
    &#160;
  </div>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">Net sales&#160;increased in the&#160;nine months ended&#160;March 31, 2026&#160;by $95.3&#160;million&#160;or&#160;16.8%, when compared to the prior year period.&#160;Acquisitions accounted for increased sales of&#160;$66.9&#160;million&#160;or 11.8%, while divestitures reduced sales by $3.0 million or 0.5%.&#160;Foreign currency positively impacted sales by&#160;$5.1&#160;million, or&#160;0.9%.&#160;Organic sales increased&#160;$26.3&#160;million,&#160;or&#160;4.6%, primarily due to&#160;increased sales into fast growth markets and contributions from new products.</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 8pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt;"><b>Gross Profit&#160;</b></p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">Gross profit in the third quarter of&#160;fiscal year 2026&#160;increased to $91.9&#160;million, or a gross margin of 40.9%, as compared to $82.4 million, or a gross margin of 39.7%, in the third quarter of fiscal year 2025. The margin&#160;increase&#160;was a&#160;result of the&#160;continued focus on pricing disciplines and productivity actions.&#160;</p>

  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b>Selling, General, and Administrative Expenses</b></p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">Selling, General, and Administrative (&#8220;SG&amp;A&#8221;) expenses&#160;for the third quarter of fiscal year 2026&#160;increased to $52.4 million, or&#160;23.3%&#160;of sales as&#160;compared to $52.0 million, or&#160;25.1% of sales during the prior year quarter.&#160;SG&amp;A expenses during the third quarter of fiscal year 2026&#160;were primarily impacted by increased expenses due to the recent acquisitions,&#160;and higher U.S. medical costs&#160;as compared to the&#160;prior year quarter.</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">SG&amp;A&#160;expenses&#160;for the nine months ended&#160;March 31, 2026&#160;increased to $162.4&#160;million, or&#160;24.5%&#160;of sales as&#160;compared to $140.8 million, or&#160;24.8%&#160;of sales during the prior year period.&#160;SG&amp;A expenses during the nine months ended&#160;March 31, 2026&#160;were primarily impacted by increased expenses due to the recent acquisitions, research and development,&#160;and higher U.S. medical costs&#160;as compared to the&#160;prior year period.</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left"><b>Restructuring Costs</b></p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">We incurred restructuring expenses of $3.0 million in&#160;the third&#160;quarter of fiscal year 2026, and $9.4&#160;million in the first nine&#160;months of fiscal year&#160;2026 primarily related to facility rationalization activities&#160;and announced closure of four sites in our Engraving &amp;&#160;Hydraulics segment.&#160;We expect to continue seeing realization of these restructuring actions during the last quarter of&#160;fiscal year 2026 and into fiscal year 2027.</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt;"><b>Deal Related Costs</b></p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">We incurred deal&#160;related expenses of $2.5&#160;million in&#160;the third&#160;quarter of fiscal year 2026&#160;and $3.6&#160;million in the first nine&#160;months of fiscal year 2026. Deal&#160;related expenses primarily&#160;consist of costs related to due diligence, advisory, legal, integration, and valuation activities associated with&#160;recent&#160;or pending acquisitions or divestitures transactions.</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 8pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 8pt; text-indent: -9pt;"><b>Gain on Sale of Business</b></p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 8pt; text-indent: -9pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">We recorded a gain on the sale of Federal Industries business of $56.8 million in the third quarter of fiscal year 2026. The sale transaction and financial results of Federal Industries are classified as continuing operations in the consolidated financial statements.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><b>Income from Operations</b></p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">Income from operations for the third quarter&#160;of fiscal year 2026&#160;was $90.8 million, compared to $26.3 million during the prior year quarter.&#160;The increase&#160;of $64.6 million, or 246.0%, is primarily due to the gain on&#160;the divestiture of Federal Industries,&#160;contributions from&#160;recent acquisitions,&#160;productivity improvement initiatives, and lower purchase accounting costs, partially offset by increase in administrative and research and development expenses.</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">Income from operations for the nine months ended&#160;March 31, 2026&#160;was $156.0&#160;million, compared to $58.8&#160;million during the prior year period.&#160;The increase&#160;of $97.2&#160;million, or 165.3%, is primarily due to the&#160;gain on&#160;the divestiture of Federal Industries,&#160;effects of&#160;recent acquisitions,&#160;productivity improvement initiatives, and lower purchase accounting and deal&#160;related costs, partially offset by increase in administrative and research and development expenses.</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><b>Interest Expense</b></p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">Interest expense for the&#160;third quarter&#160;of fiscal year 2026&#160;was $7.3 million, a&#160;decline&#160;of $1.0 million from the prior year quarter, due primarily to lower average debt balance, more favorable interest rates and a favorable interest rate swap.&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">Interest expense for the&#160;nine months ended&#160;March 31, 2026&#160;was $24.2&#160;million, an increase&#160;of $9.2 million from the prior year period due&#160;primarily to higher average debt balance&#160;as compared to the prior year period as debt was used to finance the second and third quarter fiscal 2025 acquisitions.&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">Our effective interest rate for&#160;the nine&#160;months ended March 31, 2026 was 5.80%.</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>

  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt;"><b>Income Taxes</b></p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><br/> The Company's effective tax rate from continuing operations for the third quarter&#160;of fiscal year 2026&#160;and for the&#160;nine months ended March 31, 2026&#160;was&#160;17.0%&#160;and&#160;19.7%, respectively, compared with -29.6%&#160;and 1.1%&#160;for the prior year quarter and prior year period, respectively.</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">The&#160;tax rate was impacted in the&#160;three and nine months ended&#160;March 31, 2026 by the following items: (i) the recognition of a discrete tax benefit of approximately $6 million related to the release of a valuation allowance previously recorded against the capital loss carryforward deferred tax asset, due to the utilization of such carryforward in connection with the divestiture of Federal Industries; (ii) changes in the geographic mix of earnings; (iii) foreign withholding taxes; and (iv) federal tax credits related to research and development activities.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">The tax rate was impacted in the &#160;three and nine months ended&#160; March 31, 2025&#160;by the following items: (i) a discrete tax benefit related to the release of a previously recorded tax reserve for a one-time tax charge on historical foreign earnings, as the relevant statute of limitations expired during the quarter; (ii) the jurisdictional mix of earnings; (iii) foreign withholding taxes; and (iv) federal research and development tax credits.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt;"><b style="font-size: 10pt; text-align: justify;">Backlog</b></p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><b>&#160;</b></p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">Backlog includes all active or open orders for goods and services. Backlog also includes any future deliveries based on executed customer contracts, so long as such deliveries are based on agreed upon delivery schedules. Backlog orders are not necessarily an indicator of future sales levels because of variations in lead times and customer production demand pull systems, with the exception of Aerospace &amp; Defense.&#160;Customers may delay delivery of products or cancel orders prior to shipment, subject to possible cancellation penalties. Due to the nature of long-term agreements in the&#160;Aerospace &amp;&#160;Defense segment, the timing of orders and delivery dates can vary considerably resulting in significant backlog changes from one period to another.&#160;</p>

  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">Net&#160;sales in the third quarter of fiscal year 2026&#160;increased $8.4&#160;million, or 7.6%, when compared to the prior year quarter. Organic sales increased by&#160;$7.5 million, or 6.8%, due to sales into fast growth markets and increased&#160;new product sales. Foreign currency impact increased net sales by 0.8% as&#160;compared to the prior year quarter.</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">Income from operations in the third quarter of fiscal year 2026&#160;increased&#160;by $6.2&#160;million, or 24.3%, when compared to the prior year quarter. The operating income&#160;increase&#160;was the result of higher volume,&#160;pricing initiatives and product mix, partially offset by growth investments.&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">Net&#160;sales in the nine months ended&#160;March 31, 2026&#160;increased $61.0&#160;million, or 21.4%, when compared to the prior year period. The recent acquisitions&#160;added $44.5&#160;million, or 15.6%, in sales for the nine months ended&#160;March 31, 2026. Organic sales increased by&#160;$15.3 million, or 5.4%, due to sales into fast growth markets and increased&#160;new product sales. Foreign currency impact increased net sales by 0.4% as&#160;compared to the prior year period.</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">Income from operations in the nine months ended&#160;March 31, 2026&#160;increased&#160;by $29.8&#160;million, or 49.7%, when compared to the prior year period. The operating income increase&#160;was the result of higher volume,&#160;pricing initiatives and product mix, partially offset by growth investments.</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><br/> In the fourth quarter of fiscal year 2026, on a sequential basis, we expect&#160;slightly to moderately higher revenue reflecting higher sales into fast growth end markets and increased new product sales.&#160;The Company expects slightly&#160;higher&#160;operating margin due to higher revenue, partially offset by continued&#160;growth investments.</p>

  <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">Net&#160;sales in the third quarter of fiscal year 2026&#160;increased by $9.2 million, or 33.7%, when compared to the prior year quarter. Sales&#160;increase was attributable to the&#160;acquisition of McStarlite which added $3.3 million to revenue and an organic sales increase of $5.7 million or 20.8% primarily driven by increased projects activity in commercialization of space end market. Foreign currency impact increased net sales by 0.7% as&#160;compared to the prior year quarter.</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">Income from operations in the third quarter of fiscal year 2026&#160;increased by $2.4&#160;million, or 70.9%,&#160;when compared to the prior year quarter.&#160;The&#160;increase in operating income was a&#160;result of higher volume.</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">Net&#160;sales in the nine months ended&#160;March 31, 2026&#160;increased by $26.6&#160;million, or 37.7%, when compared to the prior period. Sales increase&#160;was attributable to the&#160;acquisition of McStarlite which added $17.5&#160;million or 24.9% to revenue and an organic sales increase of $8.6 million or 12.2% driven by growth&#160;in the space and aviation end markets. Foreign currency impact increased net sales by 0.6% as&#160;compared to the prior year period.</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">Income from operations in the nine months ended&#160;March 31, 2026&#160;increased by $2.7&#160;million, or 24.4%,&#160;when compared to the prior year period.&#160;The&#160;increase in operating income was a&#160;result of higher volume.</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">In the&#160;fourth quarter of fiscal year 2026, on a sequential basis, we expect&#160;slightly to moderately higher revenue, due to growth in&#160;new product sales and more favorable project timing, and slightly to moderately higher operating margin due to higher volume and realization of productivity initiatives.</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>

  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">Net&#160;sales&#160;in the third quarter of fiscal year 2026&#160;decreased&#160;by $0.3&#160;million, or&#160;1.7%, when compared to the prior year quarter due primarily to lower demand at academic and research institutions that were impacted by NIH funding cuts.</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">Income from operations in the third quarter of fiscal year 2026&#160;decreased&#160;by $0.2&#160;million, or 4.8%, when compared to the prior year quarter due to lower sales.&#160;&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">Net&#160;sales&#160;in the nine months ended&#160;March 31, 2026&#160;increased&#160;by $2.5&#160;million, or&#160;4.5%, when compared to the prior year period due primarily to an $4.8 million&#160;benefit from the Custom Biogenic Systems acquisition, partially&#160;offset by an organic decline of $2.3 million from lower demand at academic and research institutions that were impacted by NIH funding cuts.</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">Income from operations in the nine months ended&#160;March 31, 2026&#160;decreased&#160;$0.5&#160;million, or 3.7%, when compared to the prior year period due to organic decline partially offset by contribution from the acquisition.&#160;&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">In the&#160;fourth quarter of fiscal year 2026, on a sequential basis, we expect slightly higher revenue and similar operating margin due to product mix.</p>
