  <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">Net sales in the third quarter of fiscal year 2026&#160;increased&#160;by $1.0 million, or 2.2%, when compared to the prior year quarter. Organic sales decreased&#160;by $0.8 million,&#160;reflecting weakness for hydraulics cylinders, partially offset by slightly improved demand for engraving services in North America and Asia.&#160;Foreign currency positively impacted&#160;net sales by 4.0%&#160;as&#160;compared to the prior year quarter.&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">Income from operations in the&#160;third quarter of fiscal year 2026&#160;increased&#160;by $1.2&#160;million, or 23.4%,&#160;when compared to the prior year quarter.&#160;The operating income&#160;increase was&#160;a result of realization of previously announced productivity initiatives and restructuring actions.</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">Net sales in the nine months ended&#160;March 31, 2026&#160;increased&#160;by $7.6&#160;million, or 5.7%, when compared to the prior year period. Organic sales increased&#160;by $4.2&#160;million, or 3.2%,&#160;due to improved demand in Europe,&#160;North America and Asia.&#160;Foreign currency positively impacted&#160;net sales by 2.6%&#160;as&#160;compared to the prior year period.</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">Income from operations in the&#160;nine months ended&#160;March 31, 2026&#160;increased&#160;by $2.8&#160;million, or 15.3%,&#160;when compared to the prior year period.&#160;The operating income&#160;increase was&#160;driven by higher sales&#160;and the realization of previously announced productivity initiatives and restructuring actions.</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">In the&#160;fourth quarter of fiscal year 2026, on a sequential basis, we expect slightly lower revenue and similar to slightly higher operating margin from realization of productivity initiatives.&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>

  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">Corporate&#160;expenses in the third quarter of&#160;fiscal year 2026&#160;remained flat as compared to the prior year quarter.&#160;Corporate&#160;expenses for the first nine&#160;months of&#160;fiscal year 2026&#160;increased as compared to the prior year period&#160;primarily due to increase in variable compensation and&#160;employee medical costs.</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><br/> The restructuring,&#160;gain on sale of business&#160;and deal&#160;related costs have been discussed above in the Company Overview.&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt;"><b>Discontinued Operations</b></p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">In pursuing our business strategy, we&#160;may divest certain businesses.&#160;Future divestitures may be classified as discontinued operations based&#160;on their strategic significance to the Company. Net loss&#160;from discontinued operations was approximately&#160;$0.1 million for the&#160;three and nine months ended&#160;March 31, 2026&#160;and 2025.</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><b>Liquidity and Capital Resources</b></p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">At&#160;March 31, 2026, our total cash balance was $103.7 million, of which $81.6&#160;million was held by foreign subsidiaries. The amount and timing of cash repatriation is&#160;dependent upon foreign exchange rates and each business unit&#8217;s operational needs including requirements to fund working capital, capital expenditure, and jurisdictional tax payments.&#160;The repatriation of cash balances from certain of our subsidiaries could have adverse tax consequences or be subject to capital controls; however, those balances are generally available without legal restrictions to fund ordinary business operations.</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">Net cash provided by continuing operating activities for the nine months ended March 31, 2026, was $49.4&#160;million compared to net cash provided by continuing operating activities of $36.2 million in the prior year period.&#160;We generated $84.7&#160;million from income statement activities&#160;and used&#160;$29.9&#160;million of cash to fund working capital and other balance sheet increases.&#160;Cash provided by investing activities for the nine months ended March 31, 2026 totaled $48.2 million and consisted primarily of proceeds from the divestiture of $68.3 million and cash used for capital expenditures of $19.7 million.&#160;Cash used for&#160;financing activities for the nine months ended March 31, 2026 totaled $96.8 million and consisted primarily of repayments of borrowings of $105.0 million, cash paid for dividends of $12.1&#160;million, and treasury stock related taxes of $3.8&#160;million, and borrowings of $25.0 million.&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">Net cash provided by continuing operating activities for the nine months ended March 31, 2025, was $36.2&#160;million compared to net cash provided by continuing operating activities of $64.6 million in the prior year. We generated $75.0&#160;million from income statement activities&#160;and used&#160;$32.7&#160;million of cash to fund working capital and other balance sheet increases.&#160; Cash&#160;used in&#160;investing activities for the nine months ended March 31, 2025 totaled $493.3 million and consisted&#160;of $477.4 million for the acquisition of businesses, net of cash acquired,&#160;$19.8 million used for capital expenditures offset by $3.5&#160;million in life insurance proceeds and $0.4 million proceeds from sales of real estate and equipment.&#160;Cash provided by financing activities for the nine months ended March 31, 2025 totaled $411.4 million and consisted primarily of borrowings of $792.3 million, repayments of $362.1 million, cash paid for dividends of $11.2 million, purchases of stock of $5.2 million, and $4.4 million in related financing fees.&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <div style="font-size: 10pt; text-align: justify;">
    Under the terms of the Credit Facility, we pay a variable rate of interest and a commitment fee on borrowed amounts as well as a commitment fee on unused amounts under the facility. The amount of the commitment fee&#160;depends upon both the undrawn amount remaining available under the facility and the funded debt to EBITDA (as defined in the agreement) ratio at the last day of each quarter.&#160;As our funded debt to EBITDA ratio increases, the commitment fee&#160;increases.&#160;
  </div>
  <p style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; margin: 0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">Funds borrowed under the facility may be used for the repayment of debt, working capital, capital expenditures, acquisitions (so long as certain conditions, including a specified funded debt to EBITDA leverage ratio, are&#160;maintained), and other general corporate purposes.&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-size: 10pt; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif;"><br/> During&#160;the second quarter of fiscal year 2025, we entered into a $250 million&#160;364-day term loan with existing lenders. Also, during the period, we converted the 364-day term loan into an exercise of the accordion feature under our existing credit facilities.&#160;In connection with the conversion of the loan, we entered into a Second Amendment to Third Amended and Restated Credit Agreement. This amendment expanded the total available credit under the Revolving Credit Agreement from $500 million to $825 million.&#160;As of&#160;March 31, 2026, we used&#160;$3.1&#160;million against the letter of credit sub-facility and had the ability to borrow $188.0 million under the facility based on our current trailing twelve-month EBITDA. The facility contains customary representations, warranties and restrictive covenants, as well as specific financial covenants.&#160;Current financial covenants under the facility are as follows:</p>
  <p style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>

  <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><i style="font-size: 10pt;">Interest Coverage Ratio&#160;</i>We are required to maintain a ratio of Earnings Before Interest and Taxes, as Adjusted (&#8220;Adjusted EBIT per the Credit Facility&#8221;), to interest expense for the trailing twelve months of at least 2.75:1.&#160;Adjusted EBIT per the Credit Facility specifically excludes extraordinary and certain other defined items such as cash restructuring and deal related charges up to the lower of $20.0 million or 10% of EBITDA.&#160;The facility also allows for unlimited non-cash&#160;purchase accounting and goodwill adjustments.&#160; At&#160;March 31, 2026,&#160;the Interest Coverage Ratio was 4.54:1.</p>
  <p style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><i>Leverage Ratio</i> The ratio of funded debt to trailing twelve month Adjusted EBITDA per the Credit Facility, calculated as Adjusted EBIT per the Credit Facility plus depreciation and amortization, may not exceed 3.5:1.&#160;Under certain circumstances in connection with a Material Acquisition (as defined in the Facility), the Facility allows for the leverage ratio to go as high as 4.0:1 for a four-fiscal quarter period.&#160; At March 31, 2026, the leverage ratio was 2.18:1.</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">As of March 31, 2026, we had borrowings under our facility of $472.8&#160;million. In order to manage our interest rate exposure on these borrowings, we are party to $225 million of active floating to fixed rate swaps. These swaps convert our interest payments from SOFR to a weighted average fixed rate of 3.48%.&#160; The effective rate of interest for our outstanding borrowings, including the impact of the interest rate swaps, was 5.80%.</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">Our primary cash requirements in addition to day-to-day operating needs include interest payments, capital expenditures, acquisitions, share repurchases, and dividends. Our primary sources of cash for these requirements are cash flows from continuing operations and borrowings under the facility.&#160;We expect fiscal year 2026&#160;capital spending to be between&#160;$31.0 million and $34.0 million.&#160; We expect that fiscal year 2026&#160;depreciation and amortization expense will be between $24.0 million and $26.0 million and $15.5 million and $17.5 million, respectively.</p>

  <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">We sponsor a number of defined benefit and defined contribution retirement plans.&#160;The U.S. pension plan is frozen for substantially all participants.&#160; We have evaluated the current and long-term cash requirements of these plans, and our existing sources of liquidity are expected to be sufficient to cover required contributions under ERISA and other governing regulations.&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">The fair value of our&#160;U.S. defined benefit pension plan assets was&#160;$146.2&#160;million at March 31, 2026, as compared to $146.4 million at the most recent measurement date, which occurred&#160;as of&#160;June 30, 2025.&#160;The next measurement date to determine plan assets and benefit obligations will be on June 30, 2026.</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">Contributions of $5.4&#160;million and $6.2&#160;million were made during the nine&#160;months ended March 31, 2026&#160;and&#160;2025, respectively. We&#160;expect&#160;to pay $1.6&#160;million in contributions to our defined benefit plans during the remainder of fiscal year 2026 comprising&#160;of $1.5&#160;million and $0.1&#160;million to our&#160;unfunded defined benefit plans in the U.S. and Germany, respectively. There are no required contributions to the plans in Japan or the&#160;U.K. Any subsequent plan contributions will depend on the results of future actuarial valuations.</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-size: 10pt; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif;">We have an insurance program in place to fund supplemental retirement income benefits for two&#160;retired executives.&#160;Current executives and new hires are not eligible for this program.&#160;At March 31, 2026, the underlying policies had a cash surrender value of $7.0 million and are reported net of loans of $2.7&#160;million for which we have the legal right of offset, these amounts are reported net on our balance sheet.</p>

  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><b><span style="background-color:null">Other Matters&#160;</span></b></p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><i>Middle East</i> &#8211; The ongoing conflict and broader geopolitical instability in the Middle East, especially as it relates to the availability of Strait of Hormuz,&#160;could have an adverse impact on certain portions of our supply chain which could negatively impact sales and operating income.</p>
  <p style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><i>Tariff&#160;&#8211;</i> Several&#160;of our segments may be impacted by recent tariff announcements. While we cannot predict the impact of potential new tariffs on global trade and economic growth, our regional presence, strong customer relationships, and our disciplined approach to pricing and productivity actions position us well to manage through these challenges. We monitor the regulatory environment and continue to make adjustments whenever it is deemed necessary.&#160;Most of our supply chain is strategically located to service regional demand. We plan to continue to invest in our key strategic growth priorities while closely managing our cost structure and driving productivity and pricing actions and seeking alternate sources of supply to further reduce the impact of tariffs as appropriate.&#160;We currently are evaluating the overall impact of the United States Supreme Court&#8217;s decision invalidating certain IEEPA tariffs. There are several variables associated with the net amount of any refunds we may recognize including validation of imports eligible for tariff refund, timing of any such refunds, and associated customer and supplier discussions.</p>
  <p style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><i>Inflation &#8211; </i>Certain of our expenses, such as wages and benefits, occupancy costs, freight and equipment repair and replacement, are subject to normal inflationary pressures.&#160;Inflation for medical costs can impact both our employee benefit costs as well as our reserves for workers' compensation claims. We monitor the inflationary rate and make adjustments to reserves whenever it is deemed necessary. Our ability to control worker compensation insurance medical cost inflation is dependent upon our ability to manage claims and purchase insurance coverage to limit our maximum exposure. Each of our segments is subject to the effects of changing raw material costs caused by the underlying commodity price movements. We have&#160;experienced price fluctuations for a number of materials including rhodium, steel, and other metal commodities.&#160;These materials are some of the key elements in the products manufactured in these segments.&#160;Wherever possible, we will implement price increases to offset the impact of changing prices.&#160; The ultimate acceptance of these price increases&#160;will be impacted by our affected divisions&#8217; respective competitors and the timing of their price increases. In general, we do not enter into purchase contracts that extend beyond one operating cycle. While Standex considers our relationship with our suppliers to be good, there can be no assurances that we will not experience any supply shortage.</p>
  <p style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><i>Foreign Currency Translation</i> &#8211; Our primary functional currencies used by our non-U.S. subsidiaries are the Euro, British Pound Sterling (Pound), Japanese (Yen),&#160;Peso, Chinese (Yuan) and Indian (Rupee).</p>
  <p style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><i>Defined Benefit Pension Plans</i> &#8211; We record expenses related to these plans based upon various actuarial assumptions such as discount rates, mortality rates, and assumed rates of returns. Our&#160;pension plan is frozen for substantially all eligible U.S. employees and participants in the plan have ceased accruing future benefits.</p>
  <p style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><i>Environmental Matters</i> &#8211; To the best of our knowledge, we believe that we are presently in substantial compliance with all existing applicable environmental laws and regulations and do not anticipate any instances of non-compliance that will have a material effect on our future capital expenditures, earnings or competitive position.</p>
  <p style="margin: 0pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="margin: 0pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; text-align: justify;"><i>Seasonality</i> &#8211; We are a diversified business with generally low levels of seasonality.</p>
  <p style="margin: 0pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="margin: 0pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; text-align: justify;"><i>Employee Relations</i> &#8211; We have&#160;labor agreements with several union locals in the United States and several European employees belong to European trade unions.&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><b>Critical Accounting Policies</b></p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">The condensed consolidated financial statements include the accounts of Standex International Corporation and all of its subsidiaries. The preparation of financial statements in conformity with accounting principles generally accepted in the United States of America requires us to make estimates and assumptions in certain circumstances that affect amounts reported in the accompanying condensed consolidated financial statements. Although we believe that materially different amounts would not be reported due to the accounting policies adopted, the application of certain accounting policies involves the exercise of judgment and use of assumptions as to future uncertainties and, as a result, actual results could differ from these estimates.&#160;Our Annual Report on Form 10-K for the year ended June 30, 2025 lists a number of accounting policies which we believe to be the most critical.</p>

  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b><span style="background-color:null;"><a id="item3" title="item3" href="#"></a>ITEM 3. QUANTITATIVE AND QUALITATIVE DISCLOSURES ABOUT MARKET RISK</span></b></p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;"><b><span style="background-color:null;">&#160;</span></b></p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;"><b style="font-size: 10pt; text-align: justify;">Risk Management</b></p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">We are exposed to market risks from changes in interest rates, commodity prices and changes in foreign currency exchange.&#160;To reduce these risks, we selectively use, from time to time, financial instruments and other proactive management techniques. We have internal policies and procedures that place financial instruments under the direction of the Treasurer and restrict all derivative transactions to those intended for hedging purposes only.&#160;The use of financial instruments for trading purposes (except for certain investments in connection with the non-qualified defined contribution plan) or speculation is strictly prohibited.&#160;No majority-owned subsidiaries&#160;are excluded from the consolidated financial statements.&#160;Further, we have no interests in or relationships with any special purpose entities.&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt;"><b>Exchange Rate Risk</b></p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">We are exposed to both transactional risk and translation risk associated with exchange rates. The transactional risk is mitigated, in large part, by natural hedges developed with locally denominated debt service on intercompany accounts.&#160;We also mitigate certain of our foreign currency exchange rate risks by entering into forward foreign currency contracts from time to time.&#160;The contracts are used as a hedge against anticipated foreign cash flows, such as loan payments, customer remittances, and materials purchases, and are not used for trading or speculative purposes.&#160;The fair values of the forward foreign currency exchange contracts are sensitive to changes in foreign currency exchange rates, as an adverse change in foreign currency exchange rates from market rates would decrease the fair value of the contracts.&#160;However, any such losses or gains would generally be offset by corresponding gains and losses, respectively, on the related hedged asset or liability.&#160;At March 31, 2026&#160;the fair value, in the aggregate, of our&#160;open foreign exchange contracts was a liability of $0.2 million.</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">Our primary translation risk is with the Euro, British Pound Sterlin<span style="background-color:#ffffff;">g, Peso, Japanese Yen, Indian Rupee&#160;and Chinese Yuan.&#160;A hypo</span>thetical 10% appreciation or depreciation of the value of any these foreign currencies to the U.S. Dollar at March 31, 2026, would not result in a material change in our operations, financial position, or cash flows.&#160;We hedge our most significant foreign currency translation risks primarily through cross currency swaps and other instruments, as appropriate.</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt;"><b>Interest Rate Risk</b></p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">Our effective interest rate on borrowings was 5.80%&#160;at March 31, 2026.&#160;Our interest rate exposure is limited primarily to interest rate changes on our variable rate borrowings (currently based on a rolling 1-month SOFR) and is partially mitigated by our use of an interest rate swap agreement&#160;to modify our exposure to interest rate movements.&#160;At March 31, 2026, we have $225&#160;million of active floating to fixed rate swaps with terms through August 2028.&#160;These swaps convert our interest payments from a SOFR-based rate&#160;to a fixed rate of 3.48%&#160;on&#160;$225&#160;million&#160;of debt.&#160;At March 31, 2026, the fair value, in the aggregate, of the&#160;interest rate swaps was an asset of&#160;$0.3&#160;million. A 25-basis point increase in interest rates would increase&#160;our annual interest expense by approximately $0.1&#160;million.</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt;"><b>Concentration of Credit Risk</b></p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">We have a diversified customer base. As such, the risk associated with concentration of credit risk is inherently minimized. As of March 31, 2026, no one customer accounted for more than 5% of our consolidated outstanding receivables or of our sales.</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt;"><b>Commodity Prices</b></p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">We are exposed to fluctuating market prices for all commodities used in our&#160;manufacturing processes.&#160;Each of our segments is subject to the effects of changing raw material costs caused by the underlying commodity price movements.&#160;In general, we do not enter into purchase contracts that extend beyond one operating cycle.&#160;While we consider&#160;our relationship with our suppliers to be good, there can be no assurances that we will not experience any supply shortage.</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">The Aerospace &amp; Defense and&#160;Electronics&#160;segments are sensitive to price increases for steel and aluminum products, other metal commodities such as rhodium and copper, and petroleum-based products.&#160;We have&#160;experienced price fluctuations for a number of materials including rhodium, steel, and other metal commodities. These materials are some of the key elements in the products manufactured in these segments.&#160;Wherever possible, we will implement price increases to offset the impact of changing prices.&#160;The ultimate acceptance of these price increases, if implemented, will be impacted by our affected divisions&#8217; respective competitors and the timing of their price increases.<b><span style="background-color:null;">&#160;</span></b></p>
  <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&#160;</p>
